newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Greek Intracom to develop Sofia lottery.
newsitem.headline: Greek Intracom to develop Sofia lottery.

text.p: Greece's Intracom SA group plans to develop and boost profits of Bulgaria's sports lottery by implementing modern automated systems, its managing director said on Friday.

"Under the contract Intracom will supply, install and develop a complete information system aimed at the automation of the current games and those the lottery will choose in the future," Pericles Katsioulas told Reuters in an interview.
Intracom and its daughter firm Intralot sealed a 12-year deal with the Bulgarian sports lottery operator on September 16 and the Greek grouping will invest more than $40 million.
Katsioulas said it was the biggest investment in the field of information technology and electronics in Bulgaria since 1990.
The lottery runs a number-forecasting game and gives punters a chance to forecast the results of British soccer games.
The contract sparked a row in Bulgaria on fears that the Greek group would privatise the lottery or siphon off profits.
Katsioulas said most of the criticism came from commercial rivals.
Intracom will forego a $10 million award by the International Arbitrage Court in Paris in compensation for cancelling an earlier contract in 1993, Katsioulas said.
The project includes the installation of 6,000 terminals, 25 centres, online systems and satellite links over three years.
Under the new contract Intracom will receive five percent of the lottery's annual revenues plus 10 percent of any further revenue it generates.
"The Bulgarian sports totalisator will become the owner of the whole system and will have all the rights over the games and will receive and manage all the revenues," Katsioulas said.
